draft.text: You came in for your annual checkup and to get an update on your health.
You mentioned it has been a while since your last visit and wanted to talk about how you are feeling.
You said you have been managing depression and high blood pressure, and had a lung surgery a few years ago.
You feel generally okay, but had a tough spring with allergies and stress from your daughter moving out for college.
You mentioned your blood pressure has been harder to manage, especially on weekends when you sometimes forget to take your medicine.
You run 4-5 miles a day and sometimes feel a little short of breath and get a mild pounding in your chest, especially on humid days.
You said this usually goes away on its own and you don't feel lightheaded or have other symptoms.
Your doctor will review your medication and may consider adjusting your blood pressure medicine.
You will be advised to keep taking your medication as prescribed and to watch your symptoms.
Your doctor will schedule a follow-up to check on your symptoms and medication again.
